paper_metadata.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models for Triple Extraction with Data Augmentation
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models (KaLLM 2024)
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper fine-tunes large language models for text-to-triple extraction using diverse prompt-based data augmentation. It trains eleven approximately 7B-parameter models with HuggingFace trainers and evaluates output against test triples using type, partial, exact, and strict criteria; the authors report results that outperform ChatGPT and match or exceed GPT-4.

problem_addressed: Extract subject–predicate–object triples directly from unstructured/plain-text sentences so that text-derived facts can populate knowledge graphs, while improving contextual relation extraction and adherence to the DBpedia ontology format.

methodology.primary_family: Instruction-tuned or fine-tuned LLM methods [Review-level inference]
methodology.description: The authors construct augmented WebNLG training variants in execution order: Text2triples examples; GPT-3.5-generated extraction explanations; Triples2text reconstruction examples; and reflection examples that validate or correct generated triples. Human-written and GPT-4-rephrased instructions diversify prompts. They then apply PEFT/LoRA supervised fine-tuning with HuggingFace tooling, merge LoRA weights with each base model, run prompted inference on test sentences, and compare generated triples with reference triples under four matching criteria.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: DBpedia supplies the target schema/vocabulary for the WebNLG-focused setting: triples are intended to use DBpedia-style classes and properties, and the authors checked that training/test properties were present in DBpedia. The paper does not report a separate ontology-reasoning or decoding-constraint mechanism.

evidence.excerpt: Within the DBpedia dataset, triples are generated and represented using the DBpedia ontology as the schema.
The WebNLG dataset has been analyzed to ensure the training data is of high quality. DBpedia ontology has been used to determine if the triples/relations were consistent.

text_to_kg_stages: Graph construction [Review-level inference: extracted triples are stated to be basic KG units]
Graph validation and correction [Review-level inference: reflection examples ask the model to validate/correct triples]

input_output.input_type: Plain natural-language text/sentences embedded in model-specific instruction prompts; auxiliary augmentation tasks additionally use triples as input for triple-to-text reconstruction or text-plus-triples for reflection.
input_output.input_granularity: Primarily individual sentences; the WebNLG test set contains 2,155 text-to-triple instances. Auxiliary evaluation includes document/paragraph-oriented DocRED material.
input_output.output_representation: Linearized subject–predicate–object triples, formatted as (subject|relationship|object) / ⟨subject, predicate, object⟩; the WebNLG-focused outputs use DBpedia-compatible vocabulary.

models_and_tools: Fine-tuned open-weight LLMs including Vicuna-7B/33B, WizardLM-7B, Orca-mini variants, Llama-2 variants, LlongOrca-7B, SOLAR-Instruct-10B, Mistral-t5-7B, Mixtral-8x7B, and Platypus-30B
GPT-3.5/ChatGPT and GPT-4 as comparison systems; GPT-3.5 generates explanation augmentation data and GPT-4 rephrases some instructions
HuggingFace libraries; PEFT; LoRA; alpaca-Lora fine-tune script; autotrain-advanced using TRL SFT Trainer; evaluate package
Two Nvidia 3090 24GB GPUs; cutoff/maximum token length 1,024
datasets: WebNLG: 13,211 training instances and 2,155 test instances; basis for the principal DBpedia-style training data
WebNLG-combined-with-reflections: 52,844 entries; WebNLG-reflections-updated-instructions: fourfold original size
SKE/SKE2019 and SKE21 Chinese relation-extraction data; SKE21 has 194,747 train, 21,639 validation, and 1,150 test examples
DocRED: 5,053 Wikipedia articles, 132,375 entities, 56,354 relational facts, plus distantly supervised data over 101,873 documents

metrics: Type evaluation (TE): subject/predicate/object tags must match
Partial evaluation (PE): triples partially or completely match irrespective of tag
Exact evaluation (EE): triples match exactly irrespective of tag
Strict evaluation (SE): both triples and tags match
evaluation.setting: Fine-tuned models are benchmarked by generating non-streamed outputs with a 1,024 maximum-token limit, then comparing them to ground-truth triples. The main WebNLG test has 2,155 direct text-to-triple instances and uses the same instruction forms as training. For the alpaca-Lora fine-tune script, the authors use an approximately 85:15 train/validation split; the reported validation sizes are 6,000 for WebNLG-combined and 8,000 for WebNLG-combined-with-reflections. The paper also reports an ablation across four WebNLG training-data variants and results on SKE, DocRED, FewRel, KELM, and raw WebNLG.

value: On WebNLG-reflections-updated-instructions, Orca-mini-3-7b records F1 values of 0.753 (type), 0.738 (partial), 0.719 (exact), and 0.717 (strict), exceeding the listed GPT-4 50-sample baseline (0.714, 0.692, 0.657, 0.645) and GPT-4-0314 (0.700, 0.675, 0.640, 0.629) in that table.
Vicuna-33b achieves the highest Table 4 F1 values: 0.755 type, 0.742 partial, 0.727 exact, and 0.724 strict; it is a larger model than the focal 7B group.
On KELM, Orca-mini-3-7b achieves F1 0.879 type, 0.857 partial, 0.830 exact, and 0.826 strict; Llama-2-13b scores 0.852, 0.825, 0.785, and 0.776 respectively.
Performance is very low on DocRED: Orca-mini-3 has strict F1 0.024 and Llama-2-13b strict F1 0.002. On SKE, Orca-mini-3 has strict F1 0.827 whereas Llama-2-13b has 0.124.

[Review-level inference] Evaluating type, partial, exact, and strict matching exposes progressively stricter forms of output correctness instead of relying on one aggregate score.
